notes.title: Version 1.3 - Camera controls and bug fixes
notes.content:
Hello

We've released an update to The King's Campaign, adding in the option to change the key bindings for camera controls and fixing a couple of bugs

The changes include:
[list]
[*] Added menu for binding keys for camera controls
[*] Fixed tech related issue with not being able to train elite Cavalry
[*] Fixed tech related issue with not being able to build the Belfry/Siege Tower
[/list]

If there are any other fixes, changes, or improvements you would like us to make, then please let us know

notes.title: Version 1.2 - Improving playability and performance
notes.content:
Hello

We've released the second major post-launch update to The King's Campaign, making various changes to improve playability and performance

The changes include:
[list]
[*] Task arrow shows for single units
[*] Knocked a couple of seconds off world map loading times
[*] Updated unit flags
[*] Increased amount of wood peasants can gather from trees
[*] Houses and palisades don't show health bars
[/list]

If there are any other fixes, changes, or improvements you would like us to make, then please let us know

notes.title: Version 1.1 - Improving performance and usability
notes.content:
Hello

We've released the first major post-launch update to The King's Campaign, making various changes to improve performance and usability, as well as fixing a few issues found during testing

The changes include:
[list]
[*] Improvements to unit, building and prop visuals and performance by reworking LOD (level of detail)
[*] Updated the Options layout to improve readability
[*] Fixed issue with unit level up not saving in auto-resolve battles
[*] AI are assigned a lower level garrison when capturing cities
[*] Corrected amount of tax collected when using the Collect All option
[*] The camera no longer centres on cities when selecting them
[/list]

If there are any other fixes, changes, or improvements you would like us to make, then please let us know

notes.title: Another Update
notes.content:
Hello, we've released another small update for The King's Campaign

We've updated the initial message from the advisers when starting a new campaign to offer advice on the basics of gameplay mechanics to help players new to the game

It covers selecting cities and constructing buildings, selecting armies and training units, as well as moving armies and initiating attacks

notes.title: Steam Deck Compatibility
notes.content:
Hello, we've been looking into [b]Steam Deck Compatibility[/b] for [b]The King's Campaign[/b] and, while it may be some time before Valve do an official review, we believe the game will be at least [b]Playable[/b] on Steam Deck and the changes we've made mean that [b]Verified[/b] status is possible

The King's Campaign is a spinoff of Medieval Kingdom Wars, as it's a standalone version of the Royal Blood DLC campaign, with the other DLC added in as a bonus! As such, we can use Medieval Kingdom Wars' Steam Deck Compatibility review as a basis for improving The King's Campaign

Valve's testing shows that Medieval Kingdom Wars is Playable on Steam Deck. Meaning the game is functional on Steam Deck, but might require extra effort to interact with or configure

The areas that stopped Medieval Kingdom Wars getting Verified status are as follows:
[list]
[*] This game sometimes shows mouse, keyboard, or non-Steam-Deck controller icons
[*] Entering some text requires manually invoking the on-screen keyboard
[*] Some in-game text is small and may be difficult to read
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43875974/bc927641047f3c474424789d3b8b161b9eb389d6.png[/img]

To address these issues in The King's Campaign we've:
[list]
[*] Hidden the mouse cursor until the mouse is moved and hidden the hotkeys until a key is pressed
[*] Removed the need to enter text, so the on-screen keyboard is not needed
[*] Increased the font size used throughout the game, with an option to increase it further
[/list]

We are hopeful when the time comes for an official review we will be able to achieve Verified on Deck status for The King's Campaign

This is good news for linux users too, as the Steam Deck OS is linux based and uses Proton to run Windows games, meaning The King's Campaign should be able to run on linux using Proton too

notes.title: Battle Locations
notes.content:
In The King's Campaign there are a near endless variety of battle locations, with over 350 cities that you can defend or siege, countless battlefields between cities and even ship-to-ship combat

We achieved this through a combination of level design and procedural generation

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43875974/58e759ebaddbfb17287277acbf48916900c5b3e9.jpg[/img]

[h3]Large Cities[/h3]
There are 6 large city designs, each with European and North African variants

These are used for major cities like Paris and Fez

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43875974/1c08f505278dae891f22ccbdb96e8a210e17372f.jpg[/img]

[h3]Small Cities[/h3]
There are 20 small city designs (each with 5 levels of advancement), placed in procedurally generated surroundings with variation through:
- environs/biome (e.g. desert, oak forest)
- wall set used
- wall progression
- orientation of city
- position of city and enemy camps

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43875974/f796c2a19990109bbc2d8d2cea78d410dc2db7a3.jpg[/img]

[h3]Battlefields[/h3]
There are also battles outside of cities, where armies can encounter each other in the field

These are procedurally generated with different environments/biomes

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43875974/a6708301b1b8b88d23c12a9f460256bea6bc6615.jpg[/img]

[h3]Ship-to-Ship[/h3]
At sea, when ships transporting armies clash, the units cross on gangplanks to attack each other

Of course, mounts and siege equipment remain below decks

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43875974/19ae67196f7b99c06171b6168fd49f46d0035bb7.jpg[/img]

Overall, in The King's Campaign you should never be short of somewhere new to battle

notes.title: Coming Soon
notes.content:
Hello!

The King's Campaign is coming soon! So we thought we'd answer a few questions

[h3]What is The King's Campaign?[/h3]
The King's Campaign is a hybrid of Grand Strategy and Real-Time Strategy gameplay set in Medieval Europe and North Africa, where you play as the ruler of one of 28 kingdoms and you manage your cities, engage in diplomacy and direct your armies on the world map before plunging into battle and commanding your troops directly on the battlefield.

[h3]Do I need to own Medieval Kingdom Wars?[/h3]
No. The King's Campaign is a separate standalone version of the Royal Blood DLC campaign for Medieval Kingdom Wars, and includes the expanded map from the Greater World DLC. 
So you could buy either The King's Campaign or Medieval Kingdom Wars + DLC, but you don't need both.

[h3]What if I already own Medieval Kingdom Wars?[/h3]
If you already have Medieval Kingdom Wars then just get the DLC. It might also be cheaper to get the Medieval Kingdom Wars and DLC bundle during a sale.

[h3]What's [b]not[/b] in The King's Campaign that is in Medieval Kingdom Wars?[/h3]
The King's Campaign does not include the Tutorial Campaign, Lord's Campaign or Skirmish Mode that are part of the Medieval Kingdom Wars base game.

[h3]Who are Bad Logic Studios? I thought Reverie World Studios made the Kingdom Wars games[/h3]
Reverie World Studios is the developer behind the Kingdom Wars series, and Bad Logic Studios is a microstudio that will be working with Reverie on a number of upcoming projects. 
Bad Logic Studios are the ones who have set up this version of the game.
The founder of Bad Logic Studios is someone who has worked extensively on all the Kingdom Wars games, including all DLCs and expansions
